title: Yeni BMW 3-Series ve elektrikli i3 modellerinin detayları açıklandı
summary: BMW, sekizinci nesil yeni 3-Series ailesini ve elektrikli sedan modeli i3'ü tanıttı. Yeni benzinli ve elektrikli modellerin fiyat ve menzil bilgileri de netleşti.
body:
BMW, uzun süredir merakla beklenen sekizinci nesil yeni BMW 3-Series modellerini ve tamamen elektrikli kardeş modeli i3'ü resmen görücüye çıkardı. Motor1 ve Carscoops'un aktardığına göre, benzinli yeni 3-Series ailesi ABD'de iki motor seçeneğiyle satışa çıkmaya hazırlanırken, Avrupa pazarında ise geleneksel dizel motor seçeneklerine veda ediliyor. Şirket, Avrupa pazarında 2027 model yılıyla birlikte 320d ve M340d gibi dizel varyantların satıştan kaldırılacağını doğruladı.

## i3 özellikleri ve fiyatı

**The Verge** aktardığına göre tamamen elektrikli i3 50 xDrive, ABD'de 61.500 dolarlık başlangıç fiyatı ve 1.350 dolarlık varış ücretiyle 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde raflardaki yerini alacak. Çift elektrik motoruyla toplam 463 beygir güç üreten araç, EPA testlerine göre yaklaşık 468 mil menzil sunuyor. Yeni nesil Gen6 silindirik batarya hücreleri kullanan i3, çift yönlü şarj teknolojisinin yanı sıra yenilenmiş **Panoramic iDrive** bilgi-eğlence sistemi ve Amazon Alexa entegrasyonu gibi yapay zeka destekli özelliklerle donatıldı.

## Benzinli modeller ve M350 xDrive

Benzinli motor seçeneğiyle gelen 3-Series, güncellenmiş CLAR platformu üzerine inşa edildi. Ailenin en tepe noktasında yer alan M350 xDrive versiyonu, 4,0 litrelik turbo beslemeli altı silindirli hibrit motoruyla 437 beygir güç üretiyor ve 0'dan 60 mph hıza 3,9 saniyede ulaşıyor. 2,0 litrelik dört silindirli 330 ve 330 xDrive modelleri ise 255 beygir güç sunarken, benzinli 3-Series ailesinin tüm varyantları 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde ABD'de satışa sunulacak.

**Neden önemli?** BMW'nin çoklu güç aktarma organı stratejisi doğrultusunda hem benzinli hem elektrikli hem de hibrit seçenekleri bir arada sunması, otomotiv sektöründeki elektrifikasyon dönüşümünün farklı pazarlarda nasıl şekillendiğini gösteriyor.

source_texts.title: BMW Is Killing The Diesel 3 Series In Europe
source_texts.summary: The BMW 3 Series is about to lose one of the powertrains that helped make it a European icon.
source_texts.text:
BMW Is Killing The Diesel 3 Series In Europe
The BMW 3 Series is about to lose one of the powertrains that helped make it a European icon.
The new gas-powered BMW 3 Series has arrived, debuting in the US with two powertrains: a turbocharged four-cylinder and an inline-six. In Europe, however, the new 3 Series is missing one very important engine: the diesel.
Two separate BMW spokespeople confirmed to Motor1 and Motor1 Germany that the 3 Series diesel will no longer be part of the European lineup. The change applies to the latest 3 Series, which arrives for the 2027 model year.
That means familiar models like the 320d and other diesel variants are officially on their way out.
Even without a diesel option in Europe, BMW is sticking with a multi-powertrain strategy for the new 3 Series. The company will continue offering gasoline engines alongside the all-electric i3.
BMW has also confirmed that a plug-in-hybrid version of the next-generation 3 Series will arrive in Europe in 2027. The automaker previously said the new 3 Series family would continue to offer plug-in-hybrid power, although it hasn't announced specific details about the new setup yet.
BMW also hasn't confirmed whether the next-generation plug-in-hybrid 3 Series will be offered in the United States.
2027 BMW 3 Series
If you're in Europe and want a diesel 3 Series, there's still time.
The current-generation 3 Series continues to offer diesel power, including the 320d. Meanwhile, the next-generation car is scheduled to enter production in the second half of 2026, with BMW currently putting its new-generation combustion-powered 3 Series through final testing ahead of its launch.
Once the new generation arrives, though, the diesel option will disappear. That means the end of the road for models like the M340d, too. BMW has already confirmed that the next 3 Series' range-topping six-cylinder combustion model will be the M350 xDrive.
For European 3 Series buyers, then, the diesel era is coming to an end.

source_texts.text:
When BMW first announced it was reimagining the i3 as an all-electric four-door sedan built on its Neue Klasse platform, it left out a lot of important details, like battery capacity, range, and price. Today, the German automaker is finally starting to fill in the blanks on the i3.
BMW’s revamped i3 boasts up to 468 miles of range
The i3 50 xDrive will start at $62,850 when it arrives in the first quarter of 2027.
Let’s start with price. BMW says the 2027 i3 50 xDrive will start at $61,500, plus a $1,350 destination fee, putting it firmly in the Mercedes C-Class segment of competition. (Back in March, we could only guess a ballpark starting price around $60,000.) We also weren’t certain when the new EV would be available in the US; today, BMW confirmed an official launch in the first quarter of 2027.
BMW also revealed new details about the i3’s motors. There are two of them — an electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM) in the rear axle that produces 322 horsepower and 321 lb-ft of torque; and an asynchronous motor in the front axle, putting out 165 hp and 188 lb-ft of torque — for a total output of 463 hp and 476 lb-ft of torque.
BMW confirmed an official launch in the first quarter of 2027.
The EESM, which serves as the primary drive axle, uses electricity instead of permanent magnets to power both its stator outer frame and rotor inner spinning part. An inverter acts as the brain of the system, converting direct current from the battery into alternating current for the motor, regulating the electromagnets, and monitoring performance to keep the motor running as efficiently as possible.
The range figures quoted in the press release are pretty impressive. Back in March, we estimated around 440 miles of battery range, but BMW says the actual estimated figure will be closer to 468 miles, based on EPA testing. BMW may have caught wind of the 2027 Mercedes EQS’s crazy range estimate of 925km (575 miles) on the WLTP cycle (which tends to be around 10–20 percent more generous than the EPA’s estimates), and figured they could do nearly as well for way less money. Honestly, it’s a pretty decent bet.
Frustratingly, BMW is still keeping mum on the i3’s battery capacity — though it does confirm that it features the automaker’s “Gen6” high-voltage battery built with cylindrical lithium-ion cells measuring 46 mm in diameter and 95 mm in height. The new cylindrical cells provide a 20 percent increase in energy density compared to the prismatic cells used in the Gen5 batteries.
The BMW i3 has a few other tricks up its sleeve, including bidirectional charging with vehicle-to-load and vehicle-to-home capabilities, an intelligent charging flap that opens when a driver approaches a known charging point, and Plug & Charge for automatic charging at 10 different charging providers.
The iDrive infotainment system represents a completely redesigned digital dashboard that replaces traditional gauge clusters with a heads-up style windshield projection. It stays visible even if you wear polarized sunglasses, and passengers can view or customize parts of it. The 17.9-inch central touchscreen presents as a free-cut display where you can drag and drop up to six “widgets” like media, weather, or navigation from the screen directly onto the windshield display. And the steering wheel uses “shy-tech” controls, in which buttons only light up when available and offer haptic feedback so you don’t have to look down while driving.
In the vein of luxury automakers racing to cram more AI features into their vehicles, BMW is integrating Amazon’s Alexa into the i3. The much-delayed, large-language model version of Alexa can handle natural, conversational requests, search for online information, or manage climate and windows naturally. (BMW has been angling to get the new AI-powered version of Alexa in its cars since 2022, but was delayed by Amazon’s long development cycle.)
When the car is parked, you can watch movies or live shows through the built-in Video app powered by TiVo (remember them?) and eventually Amazon Prime Video. The navigation system will run on BMW’s own maps, but with Google Places — points of interest powered by search data — integrated. The system runs on an Android-based platform and receives ongoing over-the-air software updates.
But if you’re looking for more performance, BMW is also offering the i3 M60 xDrive, a high-powered racing variant with M-specific lights and graphics and 21-inch Style 1067M aerodynamic wheels. That version will arrive sometime in 2027 for an unspecified price.

source_texts.title: New BMW 3-Series Gets Up To 437 HP, Arrives In The US Next Year
source_texts.summary: The proportions of the 3-Series are a little different to the electric i3, although its design is largely identical
source_texts.text:
- The gas-powered BMW 3-Series uses the outgoing model’s CLAR platform.
- BMW has only announced the 330, 330 xDrive, and M350 xDrive models at this stage.
- US sales of the three 3-Series variants will start in the first quarter of 2027.
For more than 50 years, the 3-Series has been the heart of the BMW family, long serving as a benchmark in its segment and combining all of what we love from the German brand. While SUVs have largely taken over the automotive industry over the past decade, the 3-Series lives on into its eighth generation, and this is it.
BMW unveiled the related, all-electric i3 six months ago, but only now has it unveiled the combustion model. As we suspected, and as teasers and spy shots showed, the regular 3-Series looks very similar to the i3. In fact, it may appear identical to the untrained eye, but BMW has made some subtle tweaks to differentiate the siblings.
The gas-powered 3-Series has first been previewed with the new M350 xDrive, replacing the old M340i xDrive. Its front end is mostly the same as the i3, complete with the same daytime running lights and kidney grilles, although they have been darkened and appear slightly wider. As this version has an engine that needs to be cooled, the lower bumper and air intakes are also slightly more prominent.
Compared to the i3, the hood of the normal 3-Series is slightly longer and sits lower. While the door skins appear largely identical, the shape of the rear side windows has also been tweaked. As you’d imagine, the iconic Hofmeister kink is still there. This being a sporty version, the M350 includes black wing mirrors, unique badging, and a bold rear end with darkened LED taillights, a diffuser, and quad tailpipes.
Bigger, But Lower, Than The i3
The gas-powered 3-Series appears slightly longer and wider in these photos, but that’s not actually the case. The 330, 330 xDrive, and M350 xDrive models confirmed so far are all 187.2 inches (4,754 mm) long, 72.8 inches (1,849 mm) wide, and sit 57.3 inches (1,455 mm) tall. By comparison, the i3 50 xDrive is 187.4 inches (4,759 mm) long, 73.4 inches (1,864 mm) wide, and 58.3 inches (1,480 mm) tall. The reason behind these differences is simple. The 3-Series uses an updated version of the outgoing model’s CLAR architecture, while the i3 is based on BMW’s brand-new Neue Klasse platform.
While the 3-Series architecture may be old, it gets the full suite of interior upgrades enjoyed by BMW’s Neue Klasse-based EVs. This means there’s the same odd steering wheel with large touchpad controllers and paddle shifters. There’s also the now-familiar slanted 17.9-inch infotainment display and the Panoramic iDrive system, working alongside an optional 3D head-up display.
A Cabin From The Future
Radical changes have also been made to the car’s dashboard with new materials, fabric, and lighting, not dissimilar to what you’ll find in some current Mini models. New seats also come standard, although the regular ones don’t include backrest-width adjustment or lumbar support, so shoppers will need to upgrade to the optional multifunction seats for that. The M350 xDrive is fitted with special M Sport seats with larger bolsters.
From now until the new M3 arrives, the M350 xDrive will sit at the top of the ICE-powered 3-Series family. It rocks a 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six with 48-volt mild-hybrid technology, delivering 437 hp and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm) of torque. When combined with a familiar 8-speed Steptronic transmission and all-wheel drive, this model runs to 60 mph (96 km/h) in just 3.9 seconds and through to a 130-mph (209 km/h) top speed, or 155 mph (250 km/h) when equipped with sport tires. Including a one-foot rollout, the 0-60 mph time falls to 3.6 seconds.
BMW has also confirmed details for the 330 and 330 xDrive models. They share the same 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder with 255 hp between 4,700 and 6,500 rpm and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque. While the top speeds of this duo match the M350, they need 5.9 seconds to reach 60 mph.
While the platform of the 2027 3-Series isn’t new, BMW says extensive chassis modifications have been made. At the front, it includes a double-joint spring-strut front axle, wider front and rear tracks, and new wheel and tire combinations. Standard models are offered with adaptive suspension or adaptive M suspension, the latter of which comes standard on the M350 xDrive.
Arguably the most intriguing feature of the M350 is Drift Moment. It has a silly name, but it’s very serious. In this mode, the sedan turns into a rear-wheel drive monster. For whatever reason, this mode will only become available at an undisclosed time next year and will be rolled out through a software update.
In terms of safety, the 3-Series includes Level 2 driver-assistance systems and what BMW calls Symbiotic Drive. This system allows the driver to easily provide turning, acceleration, and braking inputs without the L2 system disengaging, as is common in many cars.
BMW hasn’t announced US pricing details for the new 3-Series, but has confirmed sales of the 330, 330x, and M350 xDrive will start in the first quarter of 2027.
